agent-cost-report: Create a cost report for my available agent transcripts for the last seven complete days. Separate measured token usage from estimated prices and explain the reporting timezone.
babysit: Monitor the pull request I provide, summarize actionable review comments and CI failures, and help resolve them until the requested checks pass.
backup-setup: Inspect the configured local Claude-Mem backup setup and explain how to verify a recoverable snapshot before changing anything.
build: Plan and implement the feature I describe using the existing repository conventions. State acceptance criteria before making changes.
build-and-release: Plan the build and release of my proposed feature. Prepare and verify the changes, then identify the publication step for my review.
cavecrew: Help me split a small repository task into investigation, focused implementation and independent review, using the available agent tools.
caveman: Explain the bug and proposed fix concisely. Keep every important technical fact and remove unnecessary prose.
caveman-commit: Draft a concise Conventional Commits message for the diff I provide. Do not create a commit yet.
caveman-compress: Review this project-memory file for safe compression. Preserve all facts and constraints, keep a readable backup, and explain any external processing requirements before using them.
caveman-discover: Identify the LLM workflows in this repository and propose useful labels for measuring spend by workflow.
caveman-evidence-review: Review the available Caveman evidence for cost, latency, routing and errors without changing any configuration.
caveman-explore: Orient me in this unfamiliar repository. Locate the main modules and entry points, then summarize the relevant code paths.
caveman-help: Show me the Caveman commands and explain when to use each mode.
caveman-learn: Review my Caveman token-usage report and propose ranked fixes, explaining each change before applying it.
caveman-manage: Inspect the state of the Caveman experiment I identify and explain the next lifecycle action without executing it.
caveman-optimize: Review a Caveman optimization observation and design a paired baseline evaluation before proposing a candidate.
caveman-review: Review my diff. Give one concise line per finding with its location, problem and recommended fix.
caveman-setup: Explain how this repository could be connected to Caveman spend observability. Identify prerequisites and show the proposed configuration before applying changes.
caveman-stats: Show the usage data available for my current session and distinguish recorded usage from unavailable metrics.
ccs-align: Explain the prerequisites for the CCS Align workflow and check which local worker and memory integrations are available before running its cycle.
childhood: Verify the release I identify after publication, using the agreed observation window and reporting concrete failures or uncertainty.
cloud-sync: Check the configured Claude-Mem synchronization status. Explain prerequisites before enabling any cloud transfer.
design-is: Audit my design against Dieter Rams’ ten principles and propose a plan for the most useful refinements.
do: Execute the implementation plan I supply in phases, verifying each phase against its acceptance criteria.
handoff: Create a handoff document covering the goal, current state, changed files, failed attempts and concrete next steps.
how-it-works: Explain how Claude-Mem captures observations, injects context and stores data, using the configured environment as evidence.
investigate-first: Investigate this intermittent failure before editing. Rank hypotheses by evidence and propose the smallest useful diagnostic.
knowledge-agent: Help me design a focused knowledge base from the available Claude-Mem observations. State which integrations are required.
lean-build: Implement the smallest complete version of the feature I describe. Reuse existing code and define a clear stopping point.
learn-codebase: Learn the source structure of the project I provide and explain its architecture before proposing code changes.
make-plan: Create a phased implementation plan for my feature, including documentation discovery, dependencies and verification.
megacave: Summarize the technical text I provide in concise Classical Chinese, retaining technical terms unchanged.
migration: Plan a reversible migration for the schema or API I describe, preserving compatibility and defining rollback evidence.
mode-creator: Help me specify a custom Claude-Mem observation mode. Show its proposed types and configuration before activating anything.
oh-my-issues: Analyze the issue backlog I supply, group issues by root cause and draft a consolidation plan without posting comments or changing issues.
owner-goals: Analyze the available user-authored project prompts and summarize goals, asks and constraints with dated supporting quotes.
pathfinder: Map the codebase into feature-level flows, identify duplicated concerns and propose a clearer shared architecture.
ponytail: Solve my coding task with the smallest complete change and explain the outcome in plain language.
release: Prepare a release plan for the repository I identify. Verify versioning and readiness before any publication step.
request-progress: Summarize the progress of my available project requests, separating completed work, open tasks and missing evidence.
safe-refactor: Refactor the module I provide while preserving behavior. Establish useful verification before restructuring it.
screenpipe: Search the connected Screenpipe history for the activity I describe. Only retrieve context relevant to my request.
smart-explore: Find the relevant functions and structural relationships for my question without reading unrelated files in full.
standup: Review my available worktrees, branches or pull requests and produce a read-only status and consolidation plan.
surgical-patch: Fix the bug I describe at the narrowest responsible layer and verify the behavior that regressed.
timeline-report: Create an evidence-based narrative of this project’s development from its available Claude-Mem timeline.
ultracave: Explain my supplied technical material with maximum brevity, keeping each essential fact exactly once.
verify-and-stop: Verify the completed work against the acceptance criteria I provide. Report the evidence and stop without adding scope.
version-bump: In the Claude-Mem maintainer repository, prepare the requested version update across its release manifests and verify consistency. Do not publish yet.
weekly-digests: Summarize the available project timeline into weekly digests, separating each ISO week and retaining evidence of the work.
what-the: Explain this technical system in plain English: who uses it, what it does, where it runs, why it exists and when it matters.
wowerpoint: Turn my supplied document into a coherent illustrated slide deck. Preserve the document’s claims and identify any missing inputs.
